lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rodrigo Luiz | Lesson 17 -- More or Less
lesson.grammar_point: comparative adjectives (-er than / more ... than / better / worse)

listenings.text: Hello, Mister Luiz, this is David Chen from Java Aromatics, in Jakarta. Thank you for your e-mail. About our price: this year our vanilla is ten percent cheaper than last year. And our delivery is faster now, only twenty days to Santos. We have a new warehouse, bigger than the old one, so our stock is always ready. I can send you a sample this week. Please call me back when you can. Thank you.

Hi Rodrigo, it is Claire. I have the numbers for the third quarter. Brazil is better than in the second quarter: the cost is lower, and the deliveries are faster. Mexico is also good, but their stock is lower than yours. Only one number is worse: the price of transport. It is more expensive than last year, in all the regions. Can we talk about it on Monday? Thanks.

extra_audio.text: Claire asked Rodrigo to compare two vanilla suppliers. He looked at the prices, and the supplier in Indonesia was cheaper. Then he looked at the deliveries, and Madagascar was more reliable. He also saw that the quality from Madagascar was better. In the end he chose Madagascar, the more expensive supplier.
